vignette: A 62-year-old right-handed woman speaks fluently but her sentences are full of wrong words she does not notice, she cannot follow a two-step command, and when asked to repeat 'no ifs, ands or buts' she produces nonsense. Her strength is normal. Finger counting is missed in the right upper quadrant.
explanation: Fluent paraphasic speech with impaired comprehension and repetition is Wernicke aphasia, from the posterior superior temporal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere; the superior quadrantanopia comes from Meyer's loop in the temporal white matter beneath it, and normal strength shows the precentral gyrus of the superior division is spared.
